artifacts.summary: Confirms (via fixture and direct validator runs) the four formal research agents' skeletons currently pass validate-artifact.sh but carry none of the verbatim required-heading contract general-research-agent.md gained from abandoned project 166; rules on a single-canonical-home fix in report-format.md/summary-format.md, promoting ### Recommendations to top-level, and a cheap self-check; enumerates further sweep gaps (nix/neovim/web agents, and a larger founder/present/epidemiology domain-shaped-report gap, and seven skeleton-less research agents) explicitly left out of this record's file_scope.

memory_candidates.content: When a format-conformance contract (required headings, a validator regex, named near-misses) is added to fix a drift bug, check whether it landed in the actual standard document agents cite (e.g. report-format.md, named in every report's own Standards metadata) or only in one downstream consumer agent file that happens to restate the standard. The latter shape is exactly what leaves a fix 'half-applied': other consumers of the same standard never see it, because the standard itself never changed.

Extracting embedded ```-fenced skeletons from markdown agent-definition files for mechanical checking requires a line-based fence parser, not a naive regex like '```markdown
(.*?)
```'. The naive form's closing-fence pattern ('
```') also matches the start of the NEXT fence even when that fence carries a language tag (e.g. '```json'), silently merging two separate blocks and skipping the real target block in scan order. A parser that tracks fence state per line and only closes on a bare (no-language-tag) fence line, per CommonMark's own rule, avoids this.

skill-base.sh's skill_validate_task_artifacts sweep applies validate-artifact.sh by PATH CONVENTION (reports/*.md -> type report, summaries/*.md -> type summary), not by task_type. This means every extension's research/implementation agent, however domain-customized its report shape (e.g. a founder/present/epidemiology agent using '## Summary' instead of '## Executive Summary', or a title like '# Study Design Report'), is still checked against the generic REPORT_SECTIONS/SUMMARY_SECTIONS arrays as long as its artifact lands under specs/*/reports/ or /summaries/. A domain-specific report format is not thereby exempt from the generic conformance check.
